title: Why doesn't any browser create correspond html code for opening audiofiles

labels.name: interop
labels.description: Implementations are not interoperable with each other

body:
I do not know where I can ask for sure. But let me ask you here.

When I read the specification I found something that seemed strange to me.
The specification has a chapter: [7.8.6 Page load processing model for media](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#read-media). Content of these paragraph is the following:

> When an image, video, or audio resource is to be loaded in a browsing context, the user agent should create a Document object, mark it as being an HTML document, set its content type to the computed MIME type of the resource (type in the navigate algorithm), initialize the Document object, append an html element to the Document, append a head element and a body element to the html element, append an element host element for the media, as described below, to the body element, and set the appropriate attribute of the element host element, as described below, to the address of the image, video, or audio resource.
[Table of media elements](https://i.stack.imgur.com/KoX4m.png)

Based on what we have written, we can conclude that a unique html element is created for the media data. And everything would be fine, but in most browsers (google chrome, firefox, opera, maxthon (all latest version)), when opening an audio file by link or when opening an audio file from a computer, the following code is created:
```
<video controls autoplay name="media">
     <source src="music.mp3" type="audio/mp3">
</video>
```
What does not correspond the specifications. Here must be `<audio>` or I am not right? What can you say about this?
